summary: The arrow trap is implemented, but preflight_dotrap refuses ARROW_TRAP before the hero can trigger it. The same admission gap blocks the seen arrow trap path reached by #sit later in the recording. Add ARROW_TRAP to the preflight type allowlist and the seen-trap exception so the existing trap.c:dotrap logic decides whether the hero escapes or triggers the trap.

source.branch: A hero enters an unseen ARROW_TRAP on ordinary floor, causing hack.c movement preflight and then trap.c:dotrap to reach trapeffect_arrow_trap; after that trap becomes seen and the hero uses #sit without moving, causing sit.c:dosit to call dotrap and exercise the source seen-trap escape check.
callers: hack.c:domove_core and hack.c:spoteffects call the hero movement admission and trap-arrival path; trap.c:dotrap dispatches ARROW_TRAP through trapeffect_selector to trapeffect_arrow_trap.
sit.c:dosit calls trap.c:dotrap(trap, VIASITTING) for a trap under the hero; the current recording reaches this with the previously triggered, now-seen arrow trap.
dependencies: hack.c:requireSimpleHeroDestination corresponds to js/hack.js:requireSimpleHeroDestination and calls preflight_dotrap before the hero position changes.
trap.c:dotrap common gates and selector dispatch are already implemented by js/trap_effects.js:dotrap and trapeffect_selector.

trap.c:trapeffect_arrow_trap is already implemented by js/trap_effects.js:trapeffect_arrow_trap; its ordinary unmounted hero arm uses t_missile, dmgval, thitu, object placement, and screen redraw in C order.
sit.c:dosit corresponds to js/sit.js:dosit; both use the shared dotrap call for the trap under the hero.

evidence: The accepted queue at /home/vtjeng/development/vtjeng/teleport-contest/.cache/latest-saved-combined-queue.json (SHA-256 019311686e951c969402a82d519dcb00db6b3434d0c13e5123df0a1ba1ebe5e3) reports the first mismatch at segment 0, step 16, key h: “unsupported hero move: trap activation”; the evaluation names e2a08814ab03e27c9cd538cbe79526e43c1232f8 and compares 16/22 screens, 2,985/3,024 RNG calls, and 16/22 cursors.

The immutable recording challenges/cases/v38/v38-arrow-trap-return-projectile.session.json follows a wish-created unseen arrow trap with hero movement. Upstream trap.c:dotrap (2996-3060) reaches trapeffect_selector after the common force, air, seen-trap, learning, and reveal checks; trap.c:trapeffect_selector routes ARROW_TRAP to trapeffect_arrow_trap (1190-1249).

JavaScript js/hack.js:requireSimpleHeroDestination invokes preflight_dotrap before committing a move, and js/trap_effects.js:dotrap invokes it again before nomul(0). js/trap_effects.js already ports dotrap, trapeffect_selector, and the hero arm of trapeffect_arrow_trap, including trap->once, seetrap, missile creation, damage, and thitu order. The early preflight type allowlist omits ARROW_TRAP, causing the step-16 stop before the existing source behavior.

After the arrow triggers, the same recording issues #sit while still on the now-seen arrow trap. Upstream sit.c:dosit calls dotrap(trap, VIASITTING); trap.c:dotrap may then take its already-seen rn2(5) escape branch. preflight_dotrap also rejects seen arrow traps before this source branch, so the fix must add ARROW_TRAP to both its supported-type gate and its seen-trap exception list.

The selected scope is a divergence fix in js/trap_effects.js:preflight_dotrap, with source behavior anchored to trap.c:dotrap and trap.c:trapeffect_arrow_trap. The movement and sitting production callers are hack.c:domove_core/spoteffects and sit.c:dosit; JavaScript callers are js/hack.js:requireSimpleHeroDestination/spoteffects and js/sit.js:dosit. No arrow effect implementation or caller change is needed.
